small_guidance:
- Add larger BLOCK_S configs covering the full S=4056 in one iteration (e.g. BLOCK_S=4096 with num_warps=8/16, num_stages=2) so the reduction loop becomes a single pass and removes loop overhead.
- The conv (B=1024, C=16, ~4K spatial) likely dominates; try running it under `torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True` and pre-converting weights to `channels_last_3d` to speed it up while keeping the fused kernel.
- Remove the redundant `mean_acc` accumulator (sum_acc is already used for per-channel mean) and drop the `tl.where(mask, hs, 0)` since masked `tl.load(other=0)` already zeros tail — small ALU savings inside the hot loop.
large_guidance:
- The torch Conv3d almost certainly dominates this 8.2 ms budget — write a custom Triton conv3d kernel (im2col-style GEMM, one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile)) and fuse hardswish into its epilogue, writing directly into the (B,C,S) buffer consumed by the GroupNorm/mean kernel.
- Alternatively, fuse the conv epilogue (hardswish + GroupNorm partial sums) so that conv output is never materialized — accumulate sum/sumsq per group on the fly inside the conv kernel, then a tiny second pass finalizes mean/var and emits (B,C).
- Switch the layout to channels_last_3d throughout: it makes the GEMM-K axis (IC*kd*kh*kw) contiguous and lets the post-conv reduction coalesce across channels within a group.
